Hi Ben / Sentry renewals team —

Per our upcoming renewals for Datadog and Sentry (Q3), we need a combined operational plan covering three items before procurement signs PO:

1) Escrow / code/data escrow options — we need the vendor to confirm whether an escrow or third-party custody for our log metadata/ingestion configs is available and what the standard clause looks like. Procurement & Legal will want an initial draft.

2) Egress / archive migration economics — we are evaluating moving cold logs (>365 days) to a cold archive (ArchiveX) to reduce Datadog ingest/retention costs. Please provide egress pricing examples (per GB) and any tooling you have for bulk export. If Sentry has different export paths for traces vs. logs, call that out.

3) Retention add-on vs. self-managed archive — we need a workback for pilot migration (30TB) and a timeline to prevent service gaps. Include any known SLA or query limitations when logs are stored in cold tiers.

Can you confirm the above and share any relevant documents (pricing, export tooling, escrow template)? Also propose 30–45 minute slots next week for a quick sync with Procurement (Vivek) and Infra (Hannah).

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Ops
Redwood Inference

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick responses inline and attaching a pricing summary (Datadog_PRICING_Q3_2026.pdf).

1) Escrow: Datadog offers a standard provider continuity addendum and can work with third-party escrow (SecureVault). We typically provide a data export bundle for retention metadata and ingestion configs. I attached our standard pricing and options; SecureVault has a standard SLA for retrieval.

2) Egress: Egress fees vary by exporter and amount — for 30TB we can model a bulk export path to minimize egress impact. Typical egress is ~0.02 USD/GB for standard exports; if you use our managed bulk export service the per-GB fee can be negotiated or waived under reserved capacity. Note: large exports will be rate-limited to protect serving.

(continued)

3) Retention add-on vs archive: Datadog’s cold storage add-on supports queryable archives with a retrieval latency SLA (hours). If you need sub-minute analytics, cold storage is not suitable; for compliance/audit retrieval and occasional diagnostics it works well and can be much cheaper than hot retention.

We can run a pilot: export 30TB to ArchiveX, set a 12-month cold retention policy in Datadog, and establish retrieval playbooks. I propose a call on Tuesday 2026-06-22 at 16:00 UTC. If that works, I’ll loop in ArchiveX and SecureVault for their standard process.
